Android provides cameras as Linux PipeWire nodes. The platform query `capture-info` uses `$RUNGIC_PLATFORM_SOCKET`. It reports desktop visibility, camera permission and Android's cameras. While the desktop is visible and permitted, `shared/media/media-bridge.py` starts one camera source per listed camera. The command is `/usr/bin/rungic-camera-source ID WIDTH HEIGHT ROTATION FACING`.

The `camera` operation uses `/mnt/android-wayland/capture.sock`, private to the app and container. It opens the requested Android camera ID. The reply line contains camera metadata, `ok: true` and `format: android-yuv420`. Frames follow until the connection closes. Errors use {"error": string} before any frame.

Each frame starts with big-endian int32 values: magic 0x4d43414d, version 1, width, height and rotation. The three planes' row strides, pixel strides and lengths follow. Next is an int64 timestamp in nanoseconds. The Y, U and V planes follow the timestamp. `shared/media/camera-source.cpp` reads frames into a PipeWire Video/Source node.

Opening a camera shows Android's camera indicator. Thus, the provider contract check never sends the `camera` operation. Acceptance scenarios `camera.frames` and `camera.back` record frames from the front and back camera nodes on the phone, respectively.

`tools/tests/test_contract_media.py` checks `media-bridge.py` against the substitute in `tools/contracts.py`. The frame reader, `camera-source.cpp`, requires PipeWire. Acceptance scenario `camera.frames` checks that reader. Provider checks use `contract.camera` for `capture-info`, and `camera.frames` and `camera.back` for capture.
